title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat in Pune or Mumbai, say what is broken, get the landlord to have it fixed, sort out water, bills and the society, and deal politely with neighbours and noise.
intro:
Live in Pune or Mumbai for a few months and it will all happen to you: the geyser packs up, the bathroom wall goes damp in the monsoon, the water comes only from six to eight, and the people upstairs have guests till midnight. This unit gives you the Marathi to handle it — the renting words (most of them English, with Marathi endings), describing what's wrong, asking the landlord to *get it fixed*, and talking to the society and the neighbours without starting a feud.

The two skills are **complaining politely but firmly** (नळ गळतोय, जरा बघाल का?) and **getting something done by someone else**, with **करून घेणे** from the errands unit, now used the way tenants use it: प्लंबरकडून नळ दुरुस्त करून घेतला 'I had the plumber fix the tap'.

grammar.title: Complaining politely but firmly
grammar.body:
A good complaint in Marathi has three parts: **say what's wrong**, **ask** (don't order), and if needed **add some pressure** — all while keeping तुम्ही and a friendly tone.

**1. What's wrong right now** — use the spoken present continuous (-तोय / -तेय / -तंय, from करतो आहे): नळ **गळतोय** 'the tap is leaking', पंखा आवाज **करतोय** 'the fan is making a noise'. The negative is **-त नाहीये**: गिझर चालत **नाहीये** 'the geyser isn't working'. For something that has broken, use the past + **य** (= आहे): गिझर बंद **पडलाय** (m), भिंतीला ओल **आलीये** (f). Add how long with **-पासून**: दोन दिवसांपासून 'for two days'.

**2. The request** — the polite future + का: जरा **बघाल का?** 'could you take a look?', कोणाला तरी **पाठवाल का?** Or the polite command with -ऊन द्या: **पाठवून द्या**. Soften with **जरा**, **ना**, **प्लीज**.

**3. Firmness** — **-ऊनसुद्धा** (or -ऊनही) 'even after doing': तीन वेळा **सांगूनसुद्धा** कोणी आलं नाही 'even after I told them three times nobody came'. Deadlines: **आजच** 'today itself', **लवकरात लवकर** 'as soon as possible', **आजच्या आज** 'this very day'. And the classic last resort: नाहीतर मला सोसायटीकडे तक्रार करावी लागेल 'otherwise I'll have to complain to the society'.

The trap: a bare command like **दुरुस्त करा!** to a landlord or neighbour sounds rude. Ask a question (**कराल का?**) or explain the problem and let them offer.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: getting it done with करून घेणे
grammar.body:
You met this in the errands unit; around the house you'll need it constantly. Where English says 'get something fixed' and Hindi says करवाना, everyday Marathi uses the conjunctive participle -ऊन + **घेणे**: **दुरुस्त करून घेणे** 'to get repaired', **बसवून घेणे** 'to get installed', **बदलून घेणे** 'to get replaced', **स्वच्छ करून घेणे** 'to get cleaned'.

**Who does the work** takes **-कडून** 'by, from', on the oblique: प्लंबर**कडून** नळ दुरुस्त करून घेतला 'I had the plumber fix the tap', घरमालका**कडून** पैसे घेतले. Because करून घेणे can also just mean 'do it for yourself', -कडून is what makes it clear that someone else did the work.

**करून घेणे vs करून देणे**: घेणे = for yourself, देणे = for someone else. So the tenant asks: काका, जरा दुरुस्त **करून द्या** ना 'please get it fixed for us', and the landlord answers: हो, मी करून **घेतो** 'yes, I'll get it done'.

**I need to get … done**: मला … करून **घ्यायचं आहे** / करून **घ्यावं लागेल** 'I'll have to'. The ending agrees with the thing: मला नळ बदलून घ्या**यचा** आहे (नळ m), टाकी स्वच्छ करून घ्या**वी** लागेल (टाकी f), दार बदलून घ्या**वं** लागेल (दार n). In the past the ergative applies as usual: घरमालकांनी गिझर बसवून **घेतला** (agrees with गिझर).

True -व- causatives exist (बसणे → **बसवणे** 'install', करणे → करवणे), but करवून घेणे sounds bookish; in speech करून घेणे covers it.

The trap: मी नळ दुरुस्त **केला** = I fixed it with my own hands; मी प्लंबरकडून नळ दुरुस्त **करून घेतला** = I got it fixed.

culture:
In Pune and Mumbai most people rent a flat in a **सोसायटी** — a housing society with its own committee (a सेक्रेटरी and a चेअरमन), a **वॉचमन** at the gate, a monthly **मेंटेनन्स** charge and, above all, a society WhatsApp group where every complaint about parking, water timings and stray dogs ends up. In Maharashtra the rental contract is a **leave and licence** agreement, usually for 11 months and registered online; brokers usually charge a month's rent. Some landlords still prefer families to 'bachelors', or vegetarians — frustrating but common, so ask up front.

The landlord is usually **काका / काकू**, spoken to with **तुम्ही** and spoken about in the respectful plural (घरमालक आले आहेत). Complaints go by phone or WhatsApp, framed as requests: जरा बघाल का? Older neighbours may call you **तू** and ask a lot of personal questions; answer warmly. If you were the noisy ones, say **सॉरी, पुढच्या वेळी काळजी घेऊ** 'sorry, we'll be careful next time'. And Pune is famous for its **पुणेरी पाट्या** — sharp, sarcastic notices on gates and walls ('Ring the bell only once. We are not deaf.'), the city's own passive-aggressive style of complaining.

tip.title: Renting talk: English words, Marathi endings
tip.body:
- Most renting words are English: **फ्लॅट, डिपॉझिट, ॲग्रीमेंट, ब्रोकर**.
- Marathi adds the grammar: फ्लॅट**मध्ये**, ब्रोकर**ला**, तीन महिन्यां**चं** भाडं.
- 'I'll have to pay': मला **द्यावं लागेल**.
- Speak to the landlord with **तुम्ही**, and about him in the plural: घरमालक **राहतात**.

tip.title: नळ गळतोय — say what's wrong, then ask
tip.body:
- What's wrong now: spoken continuous **-तोय / -तेय / -तंय**: नळ **गळतोय**; negative: गिझर चालत **नाहीये**.
- Something that broke: past + **य**: बंद **पडलाय** (m), ओल **आलीये** (f).
- Then ask, don't order: जरा **बघाल का?**
- Firm: सांगून**सुद्धा** 'even after telling'.

tip.title: दुरुस्त करून घेणे — getting it fixed
tip.body:
- 'Get it done': -ऊन + **घेणे**: दुरुस्त **करून घेतला**, बसवून **घेतला**.
- The worker takes **-कडून**: प्लंबर**कडून** नळ दुरुस्त करून घेतला.
- For someone else: **करून देणे** — काका, दुरुस्त करून **द्या** ना.
- 'I need to get it done': मला … करून **घ्यायचं** आहे (agrees with the thing).

sentences.native: उद्या टाकी स्वच्छ करणार आहेत, पाणी येणार नाही.
sentences.roman: udyā ṭākī svachchha karṇār āhet, pāṇī yeṇār nāhī.
sentences.en: They're cleaning the tank tomorrow, so there won't be any water.

sentences.native: कचरा रोज सकाळी नऊ वाजता घेऊन जातात.
sentences.roman: katsrā rodz sakāḷī naū vādztā gheūn dzātāt.
sentences.en: They collect the rubbish every morning at nine.

sentences.native: वॉचमन काका, कोणी मला भेटायला आलं होतं का?
sentences.roman: vôchman kākā, koṇī malā bheṭāylā ālaṃ hotaṃ kā?
sentences.en: Watchman uncle, did anyone come to see me?

sentences.native: सोसायटीत पार्किंग फक्त एका गाडीसाठी आहे.
sentences.roman: sosāyaṭīt pārkiṅg phakta ekā gāḍīsāṭhī āhe.
sentences.en: In the society there's parking for only one car per flat.
The kitchen is full of cockroaches.

sentences.native: माझ्या पार्किंगमध्ये कोणीतरी दुसरी गाडी लावली आहे.
sentences.roman: mājhyā pārkiṅgmadhye koṇītarī dusrī gāḍī lāvlī āhe.
sentences.en: Someone has parked another car in my spot.

tip.title: Neighbours: ask, soften, stay friendly
tip.body:
- Older neighbours are **काका / काकू**, with **तुम्ही** — they will often call you **तू**.
- Make a complaint a question: आवाज जरा कमी **कराल का?**
- Soften with **जरा, ना, प्लीज**; if it was you, say **सॉरी** and give the reason with **म्हणून**.
- End on a friendly note: **कधीतरी चहाला या**.

sentences.native: वरच्या मजल्यावरून रोज रात्री खूप आवाज येतो.
sentences.roman: varchyā madzlyāvarūn rodz rātrī khūp āvādz yeto.
sentences.en: There's a lot of noise from the floor above every night.

sentences.native: काका, रात्री आवाज जरा कमी ठेवाल का? मुलं झोपतात.
sentences.roman: kākā, rātrī āvādz dzarā kamī ṭhevāl kā? mulaṃ dzhoptāt.
sentences.en: Uncle, could you keep the noise down at night? The kids are sleeping.

sentences.native: सॉरी काका, काल आमच्याकडे पाहुणे होते, म्हणून आवाज झाला.
sentences.roman: sôrī kākā, kāl āmchyākaḍe pāhuṇe hote, mhaṇūn āvādz dzhālā.
sentences.en: Sorry, uncle — we had guests yesterday, that's why it was noisy.
We had a fight with the neighbours over parking.
Let's not fight — let's try talking it over.
We live on the third floor — and you?
Are you new here?

sentences.native: खालच्या मजल्यावरचे काका खूप चांगले आहेत.
sentences.roman: khālchyā madzlyāvarche kākā khūp tsāṅgle āhet.
sentences.en: The uncle on the floor below is really nice.
We've moved into the new flat.
When are you moving? (to a man)
We'll need a tempo for all the stuff.
How much will the tempo guy charge?

sentences.native: रविवारी मला पॅकिंगसाठी मदत करशील का?
sentences.roman: ravivārī malā pækiṅgsāṭhī madat karshīl kā?
sentences.en: Will you help me pack on Sunday?
I've put all the books in boxes.
Send me the new address.

sentences.native: घरमालकांनी अजून डिपॉझिट परत दिलं नाही.
sentences.roman: gharmālakānnī adzūn ḍipôjhiṭ parat dilaṃ nāhī.
sentences.en: The landlord still hasn't given back the deposit.
The packing still isn't finished!
